title: Source Thinness Gate: sourceRef coverage can no longer hide one-row proof

claims.summary: A fresh deployed v0.15.34 EduTool.dev AI Governance audit proved SOURCE_REPORT.md now ships, but the package regraded at 98/A once the grader caught 56 sourceRef-covered atoms relying on one thin OpenLibrary metadata row.
proofCommands: Manual EduTool.dev ZIP/log audit saved under verification-output/edutool-audit-loop/20260620T150412Z/

claims.summary: The source-ledger grader now treats complete-looking sourceRef coverage as insufficient when many atoms rest on one thin, review-required bibliography row.

The ZIP audit helper no longer treats AI-governance model-card/model-documentation policy language as missing data-science lab assets unless actual notebook/IPYNB or local lab-asset evidence is present.
The release keeps the 100/100 target honest: the audited v0.15.34 package is progress, not complete research-brain quality, and still regrades below 100 because source proof is thin.
proofCommands: node --input-type=module <local regrade command recorded in the audit report>

carryForward.next: Build a real ResearchSession planner that researches course concepts once, caches a trusted ledger, maps retrieved source rows to CurriculumV1 atoms, and compiles many deliverables without browsing per artifact.
Bridge CourseIR atom sourceRefs directly to retrieved OpenAlex/OpenStax/OpenLibrary rows so future packages replace one-row fallback coverage with concept-relevant trusted sourceRefs.
Check whether each atom's sourceRefs are topically relevant to that atom rather than only structurally present.
